en_sense_definition: To remove from membership.

earlier_model_judge.note: 追い出す primarily means "to drive out" physically and is more informal; more precise terms for "expel from membership" are 除名する (from a group) or 放校する (from school).

en_sense_definition: A domesticated plant, in species Cucurbita pepo, similar in growth pattern, foliage, flower, and fruit to the squash or melon.

earlier_model_judge.note: The Japanese 'kabocha' is a broader category that includes pumpkins and other types of winter squash, while the Vietnamese 'bí đỏ' specifically refers to orange/red varieties.

en_sense_definition: A person with similarly overwhelming positive qualities; one who does good.

earlier_model_judge.note: All three terms can be used for this metaphorical sense of a very good person, although the Vietnamese 'thánh' might be slightly less common in this specific usage than a more descriptive phrase.

en_sense_definition: Eventually, at some undetermined time in the not-too-distant future.

earlier_model_judge.note: The Japanese 早晩 (souban) is correct but more formal and literary than the common English 'sooner or later' and Vietnamese 'sớm muộn'; 遅かれ早かれ (osokare hayakare) is a more common colloquial equivalent.

en_sense_definition: A group of people all descended from a common ancestor, in fact or belief, especially when the exact genealogies are not known.

earlier_model_judge.note: The Japanese is a loanword (クラン) which can have informal connotations (e.g., gaming), while the Vietnamese (thị tộc) is a formal, academic term matching the English definition. The native Japanese equivalent 氏族 (shizoku) would be a better match.

en_sense_definition: A long, pointed canine tooth used for biting and tearing flesh.

earlier_model_judge.note: The Japanese `牙` (kiba) is broader as it can mean "tusk" as well as "fang", while the English sense and Vietnamese `răng nanh` are specific to canines.

en_sense_definition: A hybrid martial art derived from Muay Thai, karate, and especially boxing during the 1960s to 1970s; more generally, any stand-up combat sport that combines kicks and punches.

earlier_model_judge.note: The Vietnamese 'quyền cước' is a general term for martial arts involving fists and feet, making it broader than the specific sport of kickboxing.

en_sense_definition: person whose (parent or) parents have died

earlier_model_judge.note: The Japanese '孤児' and Vietnamese 'trẻ mồ côi' both strongly imply 'child', making them narrower than the English definition 'person whose parents have died'.

en_sense_definition: overly high self-esteem

earlier_model_judge.note: The Vietnamese 'ngã mạn' is correct but is a formal, literary, or religious term; a more common equivalent like 'tự cao tự đại' would be more natural.

en_sense_definition: The smallest possible, and therefore indivisible, unit of a given quantity or quantifiable phenomenon.

earlier_model_judge.note: All three terms are the standard scientific equivalents for 'quantum'.

en_sense_definition: To embrace by holding closely, especially in the arms.

earlier_model_judge.note: All three verbs are the standard, natural terms for the act of hugging.

en_sense_definition: A dark, reddish-brown colour/color, like that of chocolate (also called chocolate brown).

earlier_model_judge.note: All three expressions are the standard and literal way to name the color 'chocolate'.

en_sense_definition: colour

earlier_model_judge.note: All three expressions are the standard, natural, and structurally similar way to refer to the color cream.

en_sense_definition: to set fire to, to light

earlier_model_judge.note: All three expressions are common and accurate equivalents for 'to set fire to'.

en_sense_definition: fruit

earlier_model_judge.note: The Japanese kanji form '茘枝' (reishi) is correct but rare; the katakana 'ライチ' (raichi) is the standard modern term.

en_sense_definition: job taken by a student

earlier_model_judge.note: All three terms are the standard, natural equivalents for 'internship'.

en_sense_definition: arthropod

earlier_model_judge.note: All three terms are the standard names for the horseshoe crab in their respective languages.

en_sense_definition: The chess piece denoted ♗ or ♝ which moves along diagonal lines and developed from the shatranj alfil ("elephant") and was originally known as the aufil or archer in English.

earlier_model_judge.note: All three terms are the standard and correct words for the bishop chess piece.

en_sense_definition: rank in a taxonomic classification between family and species

earlier_model_judge.note: All three terms are the correct technical equivalents for the taxonomic rank 'genus'.

en_sense_definition: sixth note of a major scale
ja_jmdict_glosses: la (6th note of a major scale in movable-do solfège)

earlier_model_judge.note: All three terms correctly refer to the sixth note of the major scale in solfège.

en_sense_definition: third note of a major scale
ja_jmdict_glosses: mi (3rd note of a major scale in movable-do solfège)

earlier_model_judge.note: Perfect entry, all terms are the standard solfège names.

en_sense_definition: material burnt for fragrant smoke

earlier_model_judge.note: The Japanese '薫香' is correct but is a more formal/literary term; the everyday word is 'お香' (okou).

en_sense_definition: looping

earlier_model_judge.note: Despite the poor English sense definition ('looping'), the Japanese and Vietnamese terms are perfect equivalents for the common meaning of 'knot'.

en_sense_definition: organ that synthesizes and secretes substance

earlier_model_judge.note: All three are the correct, standard anatomical terms for 'gland'.

en_sense_definition: name of the letter T, t

earlier_model_judge.note: All three terms are the standard names for the letter 'T' in their respective languages.

en_sense_definition: method of detecting a distant object by analysing radio waves which are sent towards the object and which reflect off its surfaces; field of study of this method

earlier_model_judge.note: All terms are the standard loanword for 'radar' in each language.

en_sense_definition: fourth note of a major scale
ja_jmdict_glosses: fa (4th note of a major scale in movable-do solfège)

earlier_model_judge.note: All three are the standard representations of the solfège note 'fa' in their respective languages.

en_sense_definition: complete set of chemical reactions that occur in living cells

earlier_model_judge.note: All three terms are the standard and correct words for metabolism.

en_sense_definition: one who composes music

earlier_model_judge.note: All three terms are the standard, natural words for 'composer'.

en_sense_definition: An assembly or gathering of the leaders of countries to discuss issues of international significance; also (loosely), an important or high-level gathering or meeting.

earlier_model_judge.note: All three terms are the standard and correct equivalents for a summit meeting.

en_sense_definition: governmental body with the power to make, amend and repeal laws

earlier_model_judge.note: All three terms are the correct, standard expressions for 'legislature' in their respective languages.

en_sense_definition: A lengthwise division of roadway intended for a single line of vehicles.

earlier_model_judge.note: Perfect match across all three languages for the concept of a traffic lane.

en_sense_definition: Any life form of extraterrestrial or extradimensional origin.

earlier_model_judge.note: All three expressions are the standard and natural terms for an extraterrestrial being.

en_sense_definition: A relation on sets (X,Y) that associates each element of Y with at most one element of X.

earlier_model_judge.note: This is a highly specific mathematical sense, and all three terms are the precise, standard technical equivalents.

en_sense_definition: person who comments

earlier_model_judge.note: All three terms are the standard, direct equivalents for a commentator.

en_sense_definition: To send out or give off.

earlier_model_judge.note: All three verbs are good equivalents for the action of emitting or giving off something like light or a smell.

en_sense_definition: ideology/philosophy

earlier_model_judge.note: All three terms are the standard and precise equivalents for the ideology of communism.

en_sense_definition: (mathematics) the set on which a function is defined

earlier_model_judge.note: All three terms are the standard, correct mathematical terms for the domain of a function.

en_sense_definition: positively charged nucleon

earlier_model_judge.note: All three are the standard scientific terms for a proton.

en_sense_definition: typography: / symbol

earlier_model_judge.note: All three terms are the standard and direct equivalents for the '/' symbol.
